About AI discoveries in 2025

This selection contains 308 catalog entries dated 2 Jan 2025 to 28 Dec 2025. 308 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

24 Dec 2025Children’s Hospital of Chongqing Medical University; Stanford University School of Medicine; Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital; Sichuan University; South-Central Minzu University

PROBY screening uncovers target-selective fluorescent probes for tau, BCL-2 and TDP-43

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The PROBY deep-learning pipeline screened 26,416 target-validated molecules for useful optical properties, identified 11 candidates for testing and found target-responsive probes PE859 (tau), obatoclax (BCL-2) and B3 (TDP-43). The study reports selectivity assays, cell/tissue labeling and ex-vivo tumor imaging with obatoclax. AI-guided structural modification of PE859 yielded 859-2, which enabled in-vivo two-photon and cleared-brain imaging of tau pathology in P301S transgenic mice; its measured tau-aggregate dissociation constant was 54.8 nM.

Technology: PROBY two-stage message-passing neural network pipeline (PROBY-L1 fluorescence classification and PROBY-L2 photophysical-property prediction)

Editorial relevance 60 chemistry Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PROBY ranked target-validated compounds by predicted fluorescence and seven optical properties, enabling selection and experimental verification of target-specific probes; the team then used AI-predicted structural modification alongside synthesis and bioassays to optimize PE859 into 859-1/859-2.
Test and result
The PROBY deep-learning pipeline screened 26,416 target-validated molecules for useful optical properties, identified 11 candidates for testing and found target-responsive probes PE859 (tau), obatoclax (BCL-2) and B3 (TDP-43).
Limitation / still unknown
The PROBY hits are repurposed molecules from a target-validated library, not newly synthesized compounds. Target/probe performance is assay-specific; tau in-vivo imaging was demonstrated in a small transgenic-mouse study (n=3), not humans. This entry describes probe function and imaging results, not treatment effects or diagnostic performance in patients.

A double-Lambda hypernucleus of boron-13 found with deep learning

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

The discovery comes from analysis of 0.2% of the emulsions and is based on a single event; published in Nature Communications.

Technology: Deep learning for nuclear-emulsion analysis

Editorial relevance 67 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Deep learning networks trained to recognize double-strangeness signatures selected candidate images for microscopic examination.
Test and result
Neural networks pre-selected candidate images from 0.2% of the J-PARC E07 emulsion data; microscopy and detailed kinematic analysis then confirmed one event as a boron-13 double-Lambda hypernucleus.
Limitation / still unknown
Only one event is confirmed; the estimate of more than 2,000 events in the full dataset is an extrapolation from the detection rate, and the article has no limitations section.

23 Dec 2025Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology

Machine-learning metabolomics prioritizes succinate in sepsis-associated encephalopathy

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In plasma samples from 29 controls, 32 sepsis patients and 27 patients with sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), LC–MS/MS plus machine-learning feature selection identified a 12-metabolite profile. Succinate rose stepwise from controls to sepsis to SAE, ranked among the five leading XGBoost features, and correlated with APACHE II, SOFA and lactate. In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.

Technology: Random forest and support-vector-machine feature ranking with XGBoost classification

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Machine-learning feature selection and classifier comparison were applied to the measured plasma metabolomics to identify discriminatory features; succinate ranked among the top five XGBoost features. Researchers then tested its functional relevance through supplementation in a mouse sepsis model and in cultured microglia. The animal/cell experiments were human-directed follow-up, not model-generated predictions.
Test and result
In a cecal-ligation-and-puncture mouse model, dietary succinate supplementation before sepsis worsened cognitive-test performance, neuronal injury and microglial activation; succinate also increased inflammatory gene expression in cultured microglia.
Limitation / still unknown
The human discovery cohort comprised 88 participants and the held-out model test set had 18 participants, so diagnostic performance and metabolite ranking need larger external cohorts. Succinate supplementation was given before CLP in mice, and cell experiments used a microglial cell line; these are preclinical perturbations and do not prove that succinate causes human SAE or that targeting it improves patient outcomes. Associations with severity scores are observational.

22 Dec 2025Hainan University; Guizhou University; National Institute of Agricultural Science, Rural Development Administration (Republic of Korea); Pusan National University; Kookmin University

Machine-learning prioritization and CRISPR knockout identify OsWOX13 as a rice heat-tolerance regulator

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Meta-transcriptomic comparison of heat-tolerant and susceptible rice genotypes yielded 409 meta-differentially expressed genes. Random-forest and XGBoost feature ranking with SHAP independently prioritized OsWOX13; CRISPR/Cas9 knockout lines showed lower survival under heat stress (~20% versus ~60% in wild type) and delayed flowering, with accompanying changes in ABA, oxidative-stress markers and stress/flowering-associated proteins.

Technology: Random forest and XGBoost models with SHAP feature attribution

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The models prioritized stress-associated genes from meta-transcriptomic differences; OsWOX13 was among the top-ranked genes in both models. The team tested its predicted positive role using CRISPR/Cas9 knockout, followed by heat-stress survival, flowering, physiology and proteomic assays.
Test and result
Meta-transcriptomic comparison of heat-tolerant and susceptible rice genotypes yielded 409 meta-differentially expressed genes.
Limitation / still unknown
The PubMed primary abstract supports gene prioritization and knockout evidence, but does not establish detailed direct molecular targets or field-level yield effects. Reported survival figures concern the study's heat-stress condition and experimental lines; this is not evidence of breeding performance or resilience in field environments. Mechanistic pathway interpretations remain limited to associated physiological/proteomic measurements.

21 Dec 2025Weill Cornell Medicine; Macao Polytechnic University; University of Gdańsk

CycleRFdiffusion-designed TP4 is a reproducible cyclic peptide binder to TREM2

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A structure-conditioned workflow combining CycleRFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and HighFold generated and screened 1,500 cyclic peptide–TREM2 complexes and prioritized four candidates. The lead TP4 showed weak but reproducible TREM2 binding in spectral-shift, microscale-thermophoresis and surface-plasmon-resonance assays. The authors report favorable plasma stability and moderate metabolic stability, presenting the work as an initial proof of concept for TREM2-targeted cyclic binders.

Technology: CycleRFdiffusion backbone design, ProteinMPNN sequence design and HighFold structural prediction/screening

Family RFdiffusion: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 47 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The AI pipeline generated and ranked 1,500 candidate cyclic peptide–TREM2 complexes based on structure, sequence and predicted energetics, from which four were selected for experiments; TP4 was then assessed with multiple orthogonal binding assays.
Test and result
The lead TP4 showed weak but reproducible TREM2 binding in spectral-shift, microscale-thermophoresis and surface-plasmon-resonance assays.
Limitation / still unknown
The only reported lead, TP4, is described as a weak binder. The evidence is biophysical binding and stability profiling, not demonstrated modulation of TREM2 signaling, microglial function, disease pathology or therapeutic efficacy. Treat this as proof-of-concept binder discovery.

19 Dec 2025Worcester Polytechnic Institute; University of California, Riverside; University of Massachusetts Lowell

Diffusion-guided design tests bimetallic ammonia-decomposition catalysts

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A diffusion model guided by a learned nitrogen-adsorption predictor generated bimetallic candidates near the target adsorption energy. Co75Mo25 was among the generated candidates and maps exactly to the tested Co3Mo1 ratio; under the reported supported-catalyst assay it reached 18.6 μmol gmetal⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 520 °C, about twice the paper’s Ru reference under its stated test. Co–Mo catalysts are established prior art, so this entry does not claim the first Co–Mo ammonia-decomposition catalyst or global composition novelty. Ex-situ XRD showed oxidized phases after air exposure and does not establish the working active phase.

Technology: Diffusion model guided by random-forest nitrogen-adsorption predictor

Editorial relevance 60 chemistry Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
A random-forest adsorption-energy predictor guides diffusion denoising; DFT and laboratory testing evaluate generated candidates.
Test and result
Authors report Co3Mo1 catalyst performance under a defined gas-flow, temperature, support, loading and pretreatment protocol; Co75Mo25 is the corresponding generated candidate.
Limitation / still unknown
Exact composition/formulation prior art, long-term stability, energy efficiency and scale-up remain unresolved; this draft makes no global-priority claim.

18 Dec 2025University of New South Wales; University of Western Australia; Macquarie University; Monash University; University of Michigan

AstroREG maps functional enhancer–gene links in human astrocytes

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A CRISPRi and single-cell RNA-sequencing screen tested 979 candidate enhancers in cultured human primary astrocytes and identified 158 functional enhancer–gene pairs, including enhancers regulating genes implicated in Alzheimer disease. The study trained the EGrf random-forest model on the measured screen and used it to predict additional enhancer–gene regulatory interactions genome-wide; selected model-predicted interactions were then functionally assessed by CRISPRi and qRT–PCR.

Technology: EGrf random-forest enhancer–gene interaction model, trained on the AstroREG CRISPRi/single-cell RNA-sequencing screen

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The authors used experimentally measured enhancer–gene pairs to train EGrf, then applied the model to predict regulatory interactions genome-wide. Selected predictions were followed up by individual enhancer CRISPRi and qRT–PCR. Machine learning contributed the genome-wide extension of a functional astrocyte enhancer map; the initial 979-enhancer screen itself was experimentally measured.
Test and result
A CRISPRi and single-cell RNA-sequencing screen tested 979 candidate enhancers in cultured human primary astrocytes and identified 158 functional enhancer–gene pairs, including enhancers regulating genes implicated in Alzheimer disease.
Limitation / still unknown
The primary CRISPRi screen and genome-wide model outputs are distinct evidence classes. The 158 reported enhancer–gene pairs came from the screen; genome-wide EGrf predictions are computational until tested. Figure descriptions report qRT–PCR follow-up for selected model predictions with independent duplicate transductions (n=4 per enhancer). The experiments used cultured astrocytes and do not establish enhancer causality in human Alzheimer disease or clinical relevance.

18 Dec 2025The University of Chicago; Argonne National Laboratory; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of Southern Mississippi

AI-guided experiments uncover a new polymer polymorph and improve organic transistor performance

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An AI-powered advisor in an autonomous fabrication-and-test platform guided 64 trials of mixed ion–electron conducting polymers for organic electrochemical transistors. The study reports a mobility–volumetric-capacitance figure of merit up to 1,275 F cm⁻¹ V⁻¹ s⁻¹, a 150% improvement over conventional spin coating, identifies larger crystalline lamellar spacing and greater specific surface area as favorable structural factors, and reports a previously unknown polymer polymorph.

Technology: Adaptive AI decision interface and AI advisor integrated with autonomous electronic-material fabrication and testing

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The AI advisor monitored experimental progress in real time, analyzed results and collaborated interactively with researchers to adapt the fabrication, testing and analysis steps across a data-limited campaign. The resulting AI/AE workflow guided experimental exploration over 64 autonomous trials; the model did not merely predict properties from a benchmark dataset. Human researchers synthesized polymers, fabricated devices and performed electrical and structural characterization.
Test and result
An AI-powered advisor in an autonomous fabrication-and-test platform guided 64 trials of mixed ion–electron conducting polymers for organic electrochemical transistors.
Limitation / still unknown
The primary source describes a single mixed-ion/electron conducting polymer system and an organic electrochemical transistor testbed. The reported 150% figure-of-merit improvement is relative to conventional spin coating in the study. Structural-factor associations come from a small set of ten statistically selected samples; they are not general causal rules. The new polymorph is reported in the primary paper, but the available abstract does not establish broader stability or device lifetime. The platform includes human-AI interaction and laboratory personnel performed synthesis, fabrication and characterization.

16 Dec 2025Broad Institute; and collaborating institutions

CellPaint-POSH screening links AURKAIP1 knockout with reduced mitochondrial abundance and mTORC1 signaling

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Self-supervised CP-DINO analysis of pooled Cell Painting CRISPR profiles nominated AURKAIP1 among genes with mitochondrial and mTORC1-related phenotypes. Follow-up AURKAIP1 knockout in A549 cells reduced the mitochondrial marker TOMM20 and pS6, an mTORC1 activity readout, relative to control. The authors propose that mitochondrial translation/metabolism may influence mTORC1, while the causal pathway remains unresolved.

Technology: CellPaint-POSH with CP-DINO-1640 self-supervised embeddings and a vision transformer

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
CP-DINO self-supervised embeddings and morphological similarity analysis of pooled CRISPR knockout profiles identified AURKAIP1 in a cluster with mitochondrial and pS6 phenotypes, prioritizing it for follow-up. The authors then used arrayed RNP knockout and TOMM20/pS6 staining; those assays showed reduced mitochondrial abundance and pS6 after AURKAIP1 knockout. The model enabled candidate prioritization, while the perturbation and marker measurements supplied the specific experimental evidence.
Test and result
Self-supervised CP-DINO analysis of pooled Cell Painting CRISPR profiles nominated AURKAIP1 among genes with mitochondrial and mTORC1-related phenotypes.
Limitation / still unknown
The result is from an A549 cell-line knockout study and supports an association between AURKAIP1 loss, reduced mitochondrial abundance and reduced pS6; it does not establish the molecular mechanism or direct causal pathway between mitochondrial function and mTORC1. The arrayed follow-up used two technical replicate wells per knockout, was not randomized or blinded, and is not an independent replication. The paper identifies HSD17B10 as a previously reported mTORC1 regulator; this record focuses on AURKAIP1.

The top triple mutant N155G/N218D/M222Q had reported relative activity of 753 ± 14% of wild type and also coupled biotin to a peptide fragment in water, extending beyond peptide–peptide ligation.

Technology: AI-guided enzyme mutation prediction combining binding-free-energy analysis of active-site substitutions with an experimental FRET-based rapid product-detection platform

Editorial relevance 47 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The AI-guided pipeline evaluated combinations at residues N155, N218 and M222, narrowing 7,999 in-silico variants to five prioritized mutants for FRET-based experimental validation. This reduced the candidate set and enabled selection of the N155G/N218D/M222Q variant; the AI component was applied after the paper established the wild-type aqueous amidation reaction.
Test and result
The study reports that wild-type subtilisin BPN′ directly catalyzed condensation of free carboxylic acids and amines in aqueous PBS (pH 8, 40 °C), forming a peptide-bond amide without stoichiometric coupling reagents.
Limitation / still unknown
The reported chemistry is demonstrated for specific peptide fragments and a biotin–peptide coupling example under the stated aqueous conditions; the paper does not establish broad substrate generality or production-scale utility. The 753% figure is reported relative catalytic activity with wild type as the reference, not a yield increase or 753-fold improvement. The reaction requires follow-up for broader substrate scope and process optimization.

AI contribution
The AI pipeline screened 70 candidate features from routine laboratory tests, selected a 16-feature set using multiple feature-selection methods and SHAP ranking, and combined five base classifiers in a stacking model. Test and result

Limitation / still unknown
All cohorts were retrospective and drawn from three hospitals in China; the external cohort had 545 people, including 139 Sjögren cases. The study does not show clinical impact, improved outcomes, or replacement of diagnostic criteria/clinical assessment.

Technology: Algorithmic Iterative Reticular Synthesis (AIRES)

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
AIRES used probabilistic random-forest and Gaussian-process crystallization models to guide experiment selection across linker chemistries and reaction conditions. Its greedy and batch decision rules prioritized experiments predicted to yield distinct new crystals; automated synthesis, computer-vision crystal screening and subsequent single-crystal X-ray diffraction supplied experimental outcomes for model updates and structure determination. The AI-guided campaign found structures for 10 of 48 new linkers, with twice the distinct-crystal discovery rate of random exploration.
Test and result
AIRES combined probabilistic machine-learning predictions with robotic synthesis, optical crystal screening and single-crystal X-ray diffraction to explore zinc zeolitic imidazolate frameworks.
Limitation / still unknown
This is one paper-level experimental discovery campaign. The reported efficiency comparison is against a random-exploration baseline within the study, not an independent replication. Structures were identified by single-crystal X-ray diffraction; the paper describes discovery of ZIF crystals but does not establish application performance. The campaign covered a defined single-linker Zn-ZIF chemical and reaction space, not all reticular materials.

9 Oct 2025Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Seoul National University; Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science; Hanbat National University; Korea University

Active learning discovers three high-entropy thermoelectrics with zT above 2

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A Gaussian-process model and Bayesian active-learning loop used an average thermoelectric quality factor as a physics-informed descriptor to search a nine-element chalcogenide composition space of 16,206 candidates. Across six iterations, the team synthesized and measured 80 samples; three high-entropy chalcogenides reached peak zT values of about 2.1 at 573 K, 2.3 at 473 K and 2.1 at 723 K. Atomic-scale analysis of one composition also found Cu-rich interstitial clusters and local lattice strain, proposed to contribute to low lattice thermal conductivity.

Technology: Gaussian-process regression with Bayesian active learning and a physics-informed average thermoelectric quality-factor descriptor

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The model used uncertainty-aware exploration and exploitation to select the next formulations for synthesis from a 16,206-composition design space. Experimental feedback from 80 samples across six active-learning iterations updated the Gaussian-process surrogate; model-guided selection yielded three compositions with measured zT above 2. The authors then characterized the materials and interpreted atomic arrangements and transport properties.
Test and result
A Gaussian-process model and Bayesian active-learning loop used an average thermoelectric quality factor as a physics-informed descriptor to search a nine-element chalcogenide composition space of 16,206 candidates.
Limitation / still unknown
The zT values are experimental material-property measurements, not efficiencies demonstrated in a fabricated commercial thermoelectric device. The model used the average quality factor as a surrogate descriptor and trained on only 80 samples from the large composition space; it did not experimentally test all 16,206 candidates. Proposed high-entropy segmented-element efficiencies assume idealized interfaces. The Cu interstitial-cluster mechanism is supported by microscopy/spectroscopy for the characterized sample but is the authors’ interpretation of why performance improves.

Neural-network satellite soil-moisture data expose global hotspots and pathways of rainfall coupling

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An information-flow analysis of daily observations found statistically significant local surface-soil-moisture effects on precipitation over about 15.7% of global land (60°S–60°N) in the boreal warm season, with eight regional hotspots. Sensible-heat mediation dominated most hotspots, while evapotranspiration mediation dominated two African hotspots; remote moisture availability and boundary-layer-height variability helped explain regional differences. Only four of 16 assessed CMIP6 models reproduced the ERA5-derived relationship between soil-moisture variability and causal coupling.

Technology: Neural-network-inversion satellite soil-moisture product (NNSm), analyzed with Liang–Kleeman information-flow causal inference

Editorial relevance 53 climate Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The study's long-term daily satellite soil-moisture series was generated with a neural-network inversion algorithm, extending the observed record used to map global coupling. Researchers applied information-flow analysis to this AI-derived product and precipitation observations, then cross-checked the main spatial pattern using independent ERA5 reanalysis. AI provided the satellite soil-moisture input for a concrete global climate result; the causal-inference method itself is an information-theoretic statistical technique, not a learned model.
Test and result
An information-flow analysis of daily observations found statistically significant local surface-soil-moisture effects on precipitation over about 15.7% of global land (60°S–60°N) in the boreal warm season, with eight regional hotspots.
Limitation / still unknown
The mapped effect is local surface-soil-moisture-to-precipitation information flow, statistically significant at the authors' p<0.1 threshold over about 15.7% of land; the analysis does not imply local soil moisture causes rainfall everywhere or exclude remote/upwind effects. The AI contribution is the neural-network-derived satellite soil-moisture product; the causal analysis is not itself an AI model. The spatial pattern was broadly checked with ERA5, while pathway attribution depends on ERA5-reanalysis variables and the assumptions/limitations of information-flow causal inference. Results concern boreal warm seasons and the analyzed 2003–2020 satellite period (ERA5 cross-check spans 1979–2021).

AI contribution
The researchers compared EQTransformer, OBSTransformer and PickBlue for automatic earthquake detection and P/S phase picking on continuous ocean-bottom and land-station data. OBSTransformer was selected because it detected more events than EQTransformer while yielding fewer false detections than PickBlue and closer agreement with manual picks. The transform fault is inferred from the southern seismicity pattern and selected-event focal mechanisms, not directly imaged along its full geometry; the authors describe it as possibly in an early development stage. The earthquake-processing workflow was not fully automatic: investigators manually reviewed and corrected picks, removed events recorded by fewer than three stations, and used manual focal-mechanism analysis.

After initial experimental discovery data were collected, machine-learning models ranked DrugBank candidates for transport activity. Symbolic-regression turbulence analysis separates transferable flow physics from dataset-specific closure terms

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using high-fidelity data for plane channels, zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers and adverse-pressure-gradient boundary layers, the authors used symbolic regression to decompose learned turbulence-closure corrections into inner-layer, outer-layer and pressure-gradient components. AI contribution

Test and result
Using high-fidelity data for plane channels, zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layers and adverse-pressure-gradient boundary layers, the authors used symbolic regression to decompose learned turbulence-closure corrections into inner-layer, outer-layer and pressure-gradient components.
Limitation / still unknown
The finding concerns model-derived closure components and validation on selected numerical flow configurations, not a new direct physical measurement. The claimed root cause of poor generalization is the authors' conclusion about data-driven turbulence closures in the studied context, not a universal causal theorem about all turbulence models. Out-of-sample tests and comparative RANS simulations support the stated transfer result.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The study profiled plasma and excised vegetation samples from 238 infective-endocarditis patients and 100 controls, then used an ensemble machine-learning pipeline to select a 10-protein plasma diagnostic panel. The paper reports AUCs of 0.97 in the held-out discovery test set and 0.98 and 0.94 in two external plasma cohorts. Integrating proteomic and clinical features also produced a prognostic model for severe heart-failure status (abstract AUC 0.87). LRG1 and NDUFB4 were associated with infection severity in the cohort analyses.

Technology: Ensemble machine-learning diagnostic and prognostic models; the diagnostic workflow compared six algorithms and used recursive feature elimination with cross-validation to select a 10-protein panel

Editorial relevance 53 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Machine-learning feature-importance analysis and recursive feature elimination selected a 10-protein plasma combination for distinguishing infective endocarditis from non-endocarditis samples. The models were evaluated in a held-out discovery cohort and two external plasma cohorts. A separate model combined proteomic and clinical features to classify severe heart-failure status.
Test and result
The paper reports AUCs of 0.97 in the held-out discovery test set and 0.98 and 0.94 in two external plasma cohorts.
Limitation / still unknown
The study is an observational proteomic cohort analysis; it does not demonstrate that use of the panel improves patient outcomes or can replace current diagnostic criteria. The development comparison included 238 IE patients and 100 controls, so case-control separation may not reflect performance in an unselected real-world diagnostic population. External evaluation used two additional plasma cohorts (combined n=328); the prognostic endpoint and biomarkers are associations, not causal mechanisms. The paper's proposed NET-related therapeutic implications are hypothesis-generating and are not counted as demonstrated treatment benefit.

Autonomous BTSbot-nearby follow-up captures an infant supernova’s flash spectrum and constrains progenitor mass loss

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The BTSbot-nearby system used the BTSbot machine-learning classifier to identify SN 2024jlf in ZTF data and autonomously trigger a spectroscopic follow-up request, enabling spectroscopy about 0.7 days after first light. The early spectra showed short-lived Hα, He II and C IV flash-ionization features; comparison with two radiative-hydrodynamics model grids constrained the red-supergiant progenitor’s enhanced pre-explosion mass-loss rate to roughly 10⁻⁴–10⁻³ solar masses per year.

Technology: BTSbot machine-learning transient classifier integrated with the BTSbot-nearby autonomous follow-up program

Editorial relevance 53 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
BTSbot identified the transient in ZTF alert data; host-distance and youth filters in BTSbot-nearby automatically triggered target-of-opportunity spectroscopy. This shortened latency to approximately seven minutes from alert-filter pass to first spectrum (spectroscopy was obtained about 0.7 days after first light), enabling observation of ephemeral flash features. Human and instrument teams obtained/interpreted observations; radiation-hydrodynamics models supported the mass-loss inference.
Test and result
The BTSbot-nearby system used the BTSbot machine-learning classifier to identify SN 2024jlf in ZTF data and autonomously trigger a spectroscopic follow-up request, enabling spectroscopy about 0.7 days after first light.
Limitation / still unknown
The AI contribution is event identification and automated prioritization, not inference of the stellar mass-loss physics. The rate is model-dependent and derived from two radiative-hydrodynamics code grids under adopted wind assumptions. The paper reports an individual nearby Type IIP event; this is not a population-level claim. The transient was originally reported to the Transient Name Server by a human observer, while the BTSbot-nearby program supplied rapid automated follow-up.

Editorial relevance 47 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
SISSO models learned compact descriptors of acid stability from existing calculations; model ensembles estimated prediction uncertainty, and a probability-of-feasibility acquisition strategy selected the next oxide for expensive DFT-HSE06 evaluation. The resulting feedback loop searched 1,470 candidates and identified 12 materials meeting the authors’ acid-stability criterion in 30 iterations, more efficiently than random selection.
Test and result
A SISSO symbolic-regression active-learning workflow identified 12 acid-stable oxide candidates from a pool of 1,470 within 30 active-learning iterations, using high-quality DFT-HSE06 Pourbaix calculations to evaluate oxygen-evolution stability.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a computational materials-property result, not experimental synthesis or electrochemical validation. The oxide structures were drawn from a known candidate space; the authors explicitly define “discovery” here as evaluating a previously unevaluated property, not discovering entirely new compounds. Acid stability is labeled at ΔG_Pourbaix^OER ≤ 0.10 eV/atom, a threshold that allows small positive values on the basis of potential self-passivation. The result depends on HSE06 DFT and the selected Pourbaix phases/conditions; practical catalytic stability must be tested experimentally.

AI contribution

21 Feb 2025Skåne University Hospital; Lund University; Artera Inc.; University of California, San Francisco

Prospective Swedish cohort validates multimodal AI prostate-biopsy biomarker for recurrence and adverse pathology after prostatectomy

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A previously developed multimodal AI score was retrospectively applied to archived diagnostic biopsies and follow-up from a prospectively collected Swedish prostatectomy cohort. The score, derived from digitized diagnostic prostate-biopsy images plus age, PSA and clinical T-stage, was associated with post-surgical biochemical recurrence and adverse pathology. Among 143 men with evaluable data and median 8.8-year follow-up, the continuous score was associated with recurrence (subdistribution HR 2.45, 95% CI 1.77–3.38); among 88 evaluable for adverse pathology, OR was 4.85 (95% CI 2.54–10.78). Estimated 5-year recurrence was 25% in intermediate/high score versus 4% in low score.

Technology: Artera multimodal artificial-intelligence (MMAI) prostate biomarker combining deep-learning features from digitized biopsy histopathology with age, PSA and clinical T-stage

Editorial relevance 47 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The locked MMAI score converted diagnostic biopsy images and clinical variables into patient-level prognostic scores. The prospective Swedish cohort tested whether that model-derived score associated with the distinct post-prostatectomy outcomes biochemical recurrence and adverse pathology; associations persisted after adjustment for standard NCCN/CAPRA clinical risk measures.
Test and result
A previously developed multimodal AI score was retrospectively applied to archived diagnostic biopsies and follow-up from a prospectively collected Swedish prostatectomy cohort.
Limitation / still unknown
This is retrospective external prognostic validation using specimens and follow-up from a prospectively collected cohort; it is not prospective AI-guided care, a randomized test of biomarker-guided treatment, or evidence that using the score improves outcomes. Only 143 patients had evaluable images and complete covariates, and 88 were evaluable for adverse pathology; it is a single tertiary Swedish center. The model’s earlier development setting involved men receiving radiation in North America, so this tests transport to a different population/treatment context. A 2025 conference abstract describing this cohort is an earlier presentation of the same study, not another record.

The authors explicitly describe OptPDE as a machine-learning approach. CQFinder computes the conserved-quantity objective from a symbolic PDE basis; OptPDE uses a sigmoid-smoothed objective and backpropagation to optimize 34 trainable PDE coefficients. They ran 5,000 random initializations and used dimensionality reduction to group the outputs into four families. This is a learned, trainable symbolic search, not simply use of an automatic-differentiation library.

Automatic differentiation optimized partial-differential-equation coefficients to increase the number of conserved quantities.
Limitation / still unknown
The peer-reviewed source reports four PDE families with at least one nontrivial conserved quantity and analytically examines one new candidate, u_t = u_x^3. Editorial relevance 40 medicine Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned vessel segmenters generated lumen boundaries; an ensemble and downstream lesion analysis located and quantified lesions for comparison with manual QCA and cardiologist visual estimates.
Test and result
Retrospective three-center evaluation of 1,076 selected angiography images from 420 patients. Nine view-specific segmentation models combined DeepLabV3+/EfficientNet-B4, U-Net++/EfficientNet-B4 and U²-Net; training images from 2016 were separate from 2022 evaluation data. Against blinded manual QCA, the system detected 1,705/1,828 lesions (93%) versus 69% for visual estimation; on multiple-lesion images it identified all reference lesions in 86% versus 33%.

Manual QCA is the anatomical reference, not physiological significance or clinical outcomes. Selected frames excluded occlusions and poor-quality images; only reference lesions meeting size/stenosis criteria were counted. Lesion observations repeat within patients, and reported significance does not establish cluster-adjusted uncertainty. No prospective procedural or patient benefit was tested; training details in the supplementary material were not independently inspected.

8 Jan 2025Columbia University; Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence; collaborating institutions

GET and interaction assays link a leukemia-risk PAX5 variant to stronger NR2C2 binding

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The General Expression Transformer (GET) model inferred cell-type-specific transcription-factor motif interactions from regulatory data and nominated a lymphocyte-specific interaction between PAX5 and nuclear-receptor-family factors. AlphaFold multimer modeling and PAX5 proximity-labeling in a B-ALL cell line supported interaction with NR2C2; the leukemia-associated PAX5 G183S variant showed increased PAX5–NR2C2 proximity signal. The variant-specific expression profile was enriched for predicted NR/3 and shared PAX5/NR/3 target genes, suggesting a possible regulatory mechanism for the germline risk variant.

Technology: GET (General Expression Transformer) foundation model for cell-type-specific regulatory grammar; AlphaFold2/AlphaFold Multimer for structural hypothesis assessment

Family AlphaFold: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
GET learned regulatory syntax across 213 cell types and used motif co-regulation to predict TF–TF interactions, which nominated PAX5/nuclear receptor family interactions in B cells. Structural modeling prioritized candidate binding interfaces. Researchers then used proximity labeling and mass spectrometry in a B-ALL cell line to compare wild-type PAX5 with the G183S leukemia-risk variant.
Test and result
The General Expression Transformer (GET) model inferred cell-type-specific transcription-factor motif interactions from regulatory data and nominated a lymphocyte-specific interaction between PAX5 and nuclear-receptor-family factors.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a cell-line interaction and expression analysis, not proof that the variant causes leukemia or directly alters disease risk through NR2C2. PAX5–NR2C2 interaction itself was consistent with prior evidence for the paralogue PAX2 and mouse pre-B cells; the specific reported distinction is increased interaction signal with PAX5 G183S and associated transcriptional enrichment. The authors call the disease-driving mechanism possible and identify limitations in cell-state and variant resolution.

8 Jan 2025European Space Agency (ESA), European Space Astronomy Centre

Machine-learning selection and Gaia astrometry confirm a 62-Jupiter-mass brown dwarf orbiting G 15-6

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A machine-learning search of Gaia DR3 two-body astrometric orbits flagged G 15-6 as a likely low-mass companion system. Combining Gaia’s astrometric orbit with archival radial-velocity measurements resolved the inclination ambiguity and yielded a companion mass of 62.43 (+6.16/−5.44) Jupiter masses, firmly in the brown-dwarf range. The authors identify it as the first independently validated brown-dwarf companion selected by their ML method. The radial-velocity data predate the study; the new result is the Gaia orbit and AI-guided identification that resolve the companion mass, not a newly observed companion in 2025.

Technology: Semi-supervised anomaly detection, extreme gradient boosting, and random-forest classifiers applied to Gaia DR3 astrometric-orbit solutions

Editorial relevance 47 physics Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The machine-learning pipeline ranked Gaia DR3 two-body systems for likely low-mass companions and selected G 15-6 as a brown-dwarf candidate. The Gaia astrometric orbit, combined with the independent archival radial-velocity orbit, resolved the inclination and established the companion’s mass; the models used only the Gaia orbital solutions for their candidate selection.
Test and result
A machine-learning search of Gaia DR3 two-body astrometric orbits flagged G 15-6 as a likely low-mass companion system.
Limitation / still unknown
The source study is an ML-assisted target-identification and Gaia-orbit analysis, not a 2025 direct detection. Archival radial-velocity observations already established binary motion but did not constrain the inclination enough to prove a substellar mass; Gaia astrometry supplies that missing orbital constraint. The wider candidate list includes false-positive Gaia solutions and unresolved stellar/substellar cases, which are not counted as confirmed companions here.

PRAIM: AI finds more breast cancers in German screening

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In a prospective study of over 460,000 women at twelve German sites, AI-assisted reading detected 6.7 cancers per thousand exams versus 5.7 without AI. Recall rates for further assessment were 37.4 versus 38.3 per thousand. This observational study does not show a survival benefit, and estimates of workload reduction with automated reading come from simulations.

Technology: AI support for mammogram reading (Vara)

Editorial relevance 73 medicine Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Publication status unspecified in annotation · Test context: prospective or independent check. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
AI read about half of the mammograms, marking cases as normal or suspicious, with the rest read by double reading.
Test and result
A prospective study of over 460,000 women at twelve German sites (2021-2023) compared AI-assisted reading with standard double reading by radiologists: 6.7 vs 5.7 cancers per 1,000 exams.
Limitation / still unknown
No survival benefit is shown; workload and skipped-review figures come from simulations, and the effect on prognosis is still to be studied.

The model represented homologous kynureninase sequences with protein-language-model embeddings and regressed kinetic activity to rank enzyme candidates. Four high-ranked candidates were tested in vitro and in vivo; the abstract reports one with nearly two-fold improved turnover number and reduced tumor weight in a mouse model.

Researchers experimentally tested four top-ranked candidates; the most active had nearly twice the turnover number of the prior best, and enzyme treatment was associated with a 3.4-fold reduction in tumor weight in a mouse comparison.

2 Jan 2025University of Edinburgh; University of Lille; Heriot-Watt University; University of Southern Denmark; University of Dundee; University of Southern Denmark and collaborating UK Biobank institutions

Deep learning enables multi-site bone marrow adiposity genetics in UK Biobank

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Deep learning measured bone marrow fat fraction at four skeletal sites in UK Biobank MRI data; after quality control, 48,608 participants contributed to genome-wide analyses. In the white-participant meta-GWAS, the study reported 67, 147, 134 and 174 independent significant variants for femoral head, total hip, femoral diaphysis and spine, mapping to 54, 90, 43 and 100 genes, respectively. Analyses also identified site- and sex-specific genetic associations and added signals in multi-ancestry analyses.

Technology: Previously validated deep-learning models for MRI segmentation and bone marrow fat-fraction measurement

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The study applied deep-learning models to segment four skeletal regions and derive bone marrow fat-fraction phenotypes at UK Biobank scale. Those AI-derived measurements were the phenotypes used in the study's subsequent genetic association analyses; the paper's genetic findings are not themselves outputs of a generative model.
Test and result
Deep learning measured bone marrow fat fraction at four skeletal sites in UK Biobank MRI data; after quality control, 48,608 participants contributed to genome-wide analyses.
Limitation / still unknown
The GWAS, transcriptome-wide and colocalization results are statistical associations and candidate gene mappings, not proof of causal mechanisms. Ancestry subgroup sizes differ, and results do not establish clinical utility or disease prevention. The deep-learning measurement method was established in an earlier study; this record concerns the distinct population-scale phenotype and genetic findings. A 2025 author correction fixed a misspelling of AKNA as ANKA; it did not alter the reported analysis or findings.
